story_clusters.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) supporters protested in India, marching towards Parliament House, and Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan met with Home Minister Amit Shah amid the protests. articles.title: Bengal Shifts Birth, Death Registration Authority from Local Bodies to Officials
articles.summary: The West Bengal government has issued a notification under the West Bengal Births and Deaths Act, 1969, transferring the authority for birth and death registration from local bodies to District Magistrates (DMs). DMs will now function as District Registrars of Births and Deaths, centralizing coordination at the district level. This change aims to streamline the registration process and improve administrative efficiency.

The piece is framed as a commentary on industrial transformation rather than a report on specific government actions.

The app allegedly enables communication even during network restrictions and could be misused by anti-national elements, terrorists, or cybercriminals to evade detection. The order highlights concerns over unregulated digital communication tools and their potential impact on national security and lawful interception.
articles.raw_summary: In its notice, I4C said that the app enables communication even during network restrictions and creates a substantial risk of misuse by anti-national elements, terrorist organisations, organised criminal groups and cyber criminals seeking to evade lawful detection and continue communication despite legally imposed restrictions.

It explores how this dynamic may impact Gulf nations' relationships with other global powers, including India, given the region's strategic importance for energy and trade flows.

articles.title: Oil prices hit $100 for the first time since May
articles.summary: Brent crude oil prices surged over 6% to $100 per barrel for the first time since May, driven by escalating conflict in the Middle East. The price rise raises concerns for India, a major oil importer, as it could impact fuel costs, inflation, and government budgets. The situation may prompt policy measures to stabilize energy supplies or mitigate economic effects.
articles.raw_summary: The price of Brent crude rose more than 6% on Thursday as the war in the Middle East continues to escalate.

articles.title: Trump imposes double-digit tariffs on dozens of countries as stopgap 10% levies expire Friday
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is imposing new double-digit tariffs on dozens of trading partners, including several countries, as temporary 10% levies expire on Friday. The move follows a Supreme Court ruling against his earlier tariff policies. This action could impact global trade flows and supply chains, including those involving India, by increasing costs for imported goods and potentially triggering retaliatory measures from affected nations.
articles.raw_summary: President Donald Trump is going ahead with new double-digit tariffs on dozens of U.S. trading partners just as the clock runs out Friday on stopgap levies he imposed after a stinging defeat at the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Critics warn U.S. nuclear power deal with Saudi Arabia could fuel proliferation
articles.summary: The U.S. and Saudi Arabia have agreed to a nuclear cooperation deal that could allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium, raising concerns about nuclear proliferation. Critics warn this could destabilize regional security and undermine global non-proliferation efforts. The deal involves civilian nuclear technology transfer from the U.S. to Saudi Arabia.
articles.raw_summary: The U.S. and Saudi Arabia announced a landmark deal that would give the kingdom a civilian nuclear program using American technology, and might allow for uranium enrichment in Saudi Arabia. Critics warn it could lead to further nuclear proliferation. Nick Schifrin reports and Geoff Bennett discusses more with John Wolfsthal.

articles.title: Breakthroughs in Chinese AI models threaten U.S. lead in tech race
articles.summary: Chinese companies are making rapid advancements in artificial intelligence, narrowing the gap with U.S. firms despite resource disparities. This development has drawn attention in Washington and Silicon Valley, coinciding with the White House's plan to redirect AI funding from universities to individuals to boost innovation. The discussion highlights the global race in AI technology and its potential impact on international tech leadership.
articles.raw_summary: Breakthroughs in Chinese AI models are sending shockwaves through Washington and Silicon Valley. Chinese companies are narrowing the AI gap despite vast differences in computing power and resources. It comes as the White House is planning to redirect billions in funding from universities to individuals in a bid to accelerate AI innovation. Geoff Bennett discussed more with Amrith Ramkumar.

articles.title: What to know about Iran's Pickaxe Mountain, home to an underground nuclear site threatened by Trump
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has threatened to bomb an Iranian nuclear site under construction deep inside a mountain, escalating tensions between the two nations over control of the Strait of Hormuz. The site, called Pickaxe Mountain, is still under development. The conflict raises concerns about regional stability and global oil supplies, which could impact India's energy imports and diplomatic relations.
articles.raw_summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly issued threats to bomb an under-construction Iranian nuclear site buried deep under a mountain as the two nations exchange blows over the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: AP report: Trump approves nuclear agreement that may allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium
articles.summary: The U.S. has approved a 30-year nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia that may permit the latter to enrich uranium, with U.S. firms expected to assist in developing the program. The deal raises concerns about nuclear proliferation and energy security, particularly in regions where India has strategic interests. The agreement does not involve India directly but could influence global nuclear governance and energy markets.
articles.raw_summary: The deal is expected to last 30 years and is also expected to involve U.S. firms in developing the program.

articles.title: A new threat by Yemen's Houthis could widen the Iran war and put another trade chokepoint at risk
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels have declared a blockade of Saudi Arabia, raising concerns about a wider conflict involving Iran. This could further disrupt global oil supplies and international trade, including critical chokepoints like the Red Sea. The situation may impact India's energy imports and trade routes, given its reliance on Middle Eastern oil and maritime trade.
articles.raw_summary: A declared blockade of Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthi rebels has the potential to widen the Iran war and further disrupt global oil supplies and international trade.

articles.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demanded the resignation of Education Minister Pradhan after activist Sonam Wangchuk ended a 26-day hunger strike. The government requested an additional day to respond to the demand. The incident highlights public pressure on the government regarding education policy and civil liberties.

articles.title: US to impose forced labor tariffs on many trading partners
articles.summary: The Trump administration announced new tariffs on dozens of US trading partners, including India, citing lax enforcement of forced labor bans. The move comes as a 10% global duty was set to expire. The tariffs target countries accused of not adequately addressing forced labor practices, which could impact trade flows and policy considerations for affected nations.
articles.raw_summary: The Trump administration has unveiled new tariffs on dozens of US trading partners for what it says is lax enforcement of "forced labor" bans. The new tariffs arrive just as a 10% global duty was set to expire.

articles.title: Indian activist Sonam Wangchuk ends hunger strike
articles.summary: Indian activist Sonam Wangchuk ended a 26-day hunger strike after negotiations with authorities. He cited concerns over possible nationwide violence as a reason for ending the protest. Wangchuk's strike was part of broader demands related to governance and civil liberties in India.
articles.raw_summary: Sonam Wangchuk has ended his hunger strike after 26 days, saying the decision follows a "long negotiation" on various conditions and "in view of possible violence in the country."

articles.title: Sweden eases mining permits to cut China minerals reliance
articles.summary: Sweden's government has declared the mining of critical minerals and rare earths a national security priority, allowing faster permit approvals. The move aims to reduce Sweden's dependence on China for these resources. The government stated this step was necessary to address supply chain vulnerabilities.
articles.raw_summary: Sweden has declared the mining of critical minerals and rare earths a national security interest. This will ease and expedite the permit process. The government said the step was needed to counter dependence on China.

articles.title: Oil prices jump as Hormuz, Red Sea crises deepen
articles.summary: Renewed attacks on shipping routes in the Gulf of Hormuz and the Red Sea have disrupted global oil supplies, pushing crude oil prices back above $100 per barrel. The crises involve regional conflicts and Houthi rebel activity, raising concerns about energy market stability. For India, which relies heavily on oil imports, this could impact fuel costs, inflation, and trade balances, potentially prompting policy discussions on energy security or strategic reserves.
articles.raw_summary: Renewed strikes on shipping in the Gulf and the Red Sea have dealt a fresh double blow to global oil markets, with the price of crude oil once again passing $100 a barrel. DW examines what could push prices even higher.

articles.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
articles.summary: Lenacapavir is a new HIV prevention drug that requires only two injections per year, offering a significant improvement over daily pills for high-risk groups. Its effectiveness depends on ensuring sufficient supply and reaching the intended at-risk populations. The drug's long-term impact on reducing HIV infections in India will depend on public health policies and implementation strategies.
articles.raw_summary: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

articles.title: US citizens are ramping up pressure on data centers
articles.summary: Rapid construction of data centers across the US, driven by AI demand, is raising serious concerns about environmental damage, public health risks, and strain on energy supplies. Local communities and activists have opposed or delayed several projects, citing these threats. The issue underscores broader debates about balancing technological growth with sustainability and energy management.
articles.raw_summary: Rapid data center construction across the US, fueled by AI, comes with serious threats to the environment, public health and energy supply. Local opposition has blocked or delayed dozens of projects.

articles.title: EU fines Google €890 million over competition rules
articles.summary: The European Commission fined Google €890 million for violating competition rules by unfairly favoring its own search engine and app store, harming competitors. The ruling highlights concerns over anti-competitive practices in digital markets. Google, a major global tech firm with significant operations in India, faces regulatory scrutiny that could influence policy discussions in India's digital economy.
articles.raw_summary: The European Commission said it found that Google had preferenced its search engine and app store in ways that unfairly harmed competition.

articles.raw_summary: Infertility affects one in six women in Germany. However, access to reproductive medicine is not available to all. Surrogacy as well as egg donation are banned.
